jobs.description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

We're looking for a builder to help construct a world class Growth organization. This is an opinionated leader that is motivated by creating big picture vision and digging into where the biggest opportunities are, sizing them, and building the systems, rigor, and connective tissue that let Growth and GTM operate cohesively. This is a member of Gusto's Insights & Operations (I&O) team — our internal Strategy/BizOps function — embedded against Growth, partnering closely with our Head of Growth and our CRO-side GTM leadership.

This role is intentionally IC-first. You'll start by going deep on the highest-leverage problems in Growth, build a point of view grounded in data, and drive it to outcome. As trust and scope grow, this role is expected to expand — most likely into owning the operating bridge between Growth and our broader go-to-market organization, and potentially into building and leading a small team.

About the Team:

Gusto's Growth organization is on an ambitious trajectory: we're building toward a much more self-serve-led motion, and the opportunity ahead is significant. As Growth scales, we have a chance to be much more intentional about how it connects to Product and to our go-to-market teams (sales, demand gen, expansion sales, pricing, etc) — building a shared, prioritized roadmap and clear visibility into dependencies from the ground up, rather than retrofitting it later.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Identify and size the highest-leverage opportunities for Growth: go from a fuzzy problem to a clear-eyed analysis of the opportunity, a recommendation on whether to pursue it, and a plan if the answer is yes.
  • Anchor on problems, not headcount: dig into what's actually slowing the Growth organization down, define how to build a best in class engine, size the opportunity, and decide what's worth solving before proposing who or what is needed — not the reverse.
  • Build the operating rhythm for Growth and drive execution against it: planning cycles, prioritization, and a shared, prioritized roadmap that makes trade-offs and dependencies visible across Growth R&D, Product R&D, and GTM.
  • Bring real analytical rigor to how Growth invests — attribution, LTV, and testing/experimentation discipline — so decisions about where to deploy resources are tied clearly to business impact.
  • Close the gap between Growth R&D and go-to-market: build the mechanisms (shared roadmap, dependency tracking, decision forums) that let both orgs operate as one team working toward the same number, rather than two orgs trading requests.
  • Design an operating system anchored in technology vs. humans: build the muscle and mechanisms the Growth org can through automation, and hand off ownership once a system is running
  • Act as a trusted advisor to Growth leadership: pressure-test strategy, surface risks and blind spots early, and bring an opinionated point of view, not just facilitation.
  • Use AI as a default, not an add-on: build reusable, AI-powered workflows for planning, synthesis, and reporting so manual coordination is the exception, not the norm.
  • Spot when a team is optimizing for the wrong thing: recognize when more effort against the current approach won't get us where we need to go, and push teams toward a fundamentally different path rather than a marginal improvement.
  • Raise the bar for how I&O operates, not just how Growth operates: share what's working, question what isn't, and help the broader I&O team build a stronger, more consistent craft.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 15+ years in operations, business operations, or strategy & ops at a high-growth tec

jobs.title: Retail Partner Manager
jobs.location: Bay Area, CA, United States of America
jobs.description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

The Role

As we grow Square's presence across the US Retail Channel, we're looking for a Retail Partner Manager to drive awareness and acquisition of Square at major US retailers such as Best Buy, Walmart, Target, and other large format retailers. You'll own quarterly sales and revenue goals for Square Hardware in the channel – optimizing our existing retail partnerships and unlocking new growth within them, from partner mix, placement, and promotional strategy to entirely new ways of partnering. This is a high-ownership role that requires an entrepreneurial operator: someone who navigates ambiguity and setbacks with resourcefulness, engages the right internal partners – across Supply & Demand, Growth Partnerships, Product Marketing, and Finance.

You will:

  • Own channel results: Meet quarterly sales and revenue goals for Square Hardware across US retail, tracking sell-through, forecasting, and growth initiatives tied to seller acquisition and revenue.
  • Build the playbook: Create, test, and evolve go-to-market strategies for key retailers – including approaches that don't exist yet today – moving fast from hypothesis to pilot to scaled rollout.
  • Grow existing partnerships: Own relationships with current retailers and distributor partners end-to-end as their primary contact at Square, proactively architecting new partnership models and formats rather than defending the status quo.
  • Source and sign new partners: Identify, evaluate, pitch, negotiate, and close new retail partnerships from the ground up – often with no existing relationship, internal champion, or playbook to follow.
  • Drive cross-functional execution: Lead work across Supply & Demand, Growth Partnerships, Finance, Product Marketing, and Operations on launches, weekly forecasting, and GTM readiness – proactively pulling in the right people for thought partnership when you hit a wall, rather than waiting to be told.
  • Deploy budget like an owner: Manage the retail marketing budget with a test-and-learn mindset – run scrappy experiments, read results quickly, and reallocate investment with urgency toward what's working.

You Have:

  • 5+ years in business-to-business sales, account management, or retail marketing – preferably in Consumer Electronics, with deep experience at Best Buy, Walmart, Costco, or other large-format retailers.
  • A proven track record of building a partnership, program, or channel from scratch and scaling it to success – without relying on existing playbooks or infrastructure.
  • Resourcefulness and tenacity to push through obstacles and find creative paths to results in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate with high autonomy and minimal oversight: setting your own priorities, moving with urgency, and proactively looping in the right internal partners rather than waiting for direction.
  • The ability to balance quarterly execution with a multi-quarter strategic view – and to see around the corner as the retail landscape evolves.
  • Strong analytical, structured thinking to assess business opportunities and campaign performance, balanced with comfort acting before all the data or process exists.
  • Experience managing external decision makers and influencing cross-functional teams through credibility rather than authority.
  • A BA or equivalent experience; ability to travel (~20%).

jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Our users are the heart of our business. Stripe’s Global Customer Success Team is responsible for managing our largest and most strategic relationships, such as Doordash, Lyft, and Shopify. In this manager role you’ll be responsible for a high-performing team of Customer Success Managers. You’ll lead and coach the team, helping them deliver on ambitious targets, roll up your sleeves to work directly with executives at existing enterprise Stripe customers and partner cross functionally to help users execute their business priorities.

We are looking for a hands-on, visionary leader who has demonstrated success dealing with ambiguity, operating in a high-growth environment, and solving complicated problems with limited oversight. Ideal candidates will have management and leadership experience scaling a technology Customer Success team, superior communication skills, and a track record for building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and understanding unique customer needs.

  • Recruit, develop, and lead a team of Customer Success Managers supporting strategic, relationship-based accounts.
  • Help drive an engagement model focused on building durable user relationships, increasing adoption, delivering value

The Dasher & Logistics team supports the millions of Dashers who power DoorDash’s marketplace. We are looking for an Associate, Strategy & Operations to join our Dasher Financial team. This role is about building the operations of a bank program at scale — a bank product that is already used by millions of Dashers each month.

Unlike traditional banks that feel slow and impersonal, our ambition is to build a financial product that is fast, intuitive, and genuinely supportive — one that helps Dashers not just hold money, but actively improve their financial health. Dasher Financial is an ambitious bet - building fintech products for the future of work. For someone with a strong foundation in problem solving who wants to grow into a future operator or general manager, this is a rare opportunity to learn by doing in a zero-to-one environment.

Our team is responsible for building and maintaining relationships with key partner banks to manage risk for Stripe’s business activities. These banking partnerships enable Stripe to accept and make payments, provide credit, move and store money, and develop new products and solutions to meet our users’ needs. We work across a broad range of risk and compliance topics, including credit, fraud, regulatory, financial crime, reputational, product, and operational risks.

What you’ll do

You’ll work with key banking and network partners across North America that provide bank identification number (BIN) sponsorship for merchant acquiring and card issuing. You’ll also bring experience managing risk across money transmission.

Risk management is a critical part of these relationships, and you’ll need a broad understanding of risk disciplines across merchant acquiring and banking. You’ll lead activities to improve risk management interactions between Stripe and its partners, manage key aspects of partner relationships, and execute high-impact initiatives.

You’ll work closely with internal and external stakeholders to set objectives, coordinate priorities, and drive execution. Internally, you’ll coordinate with product and engineering teams, as well as Risk, Fraud, Financial Crime & Supportability, Operations, Legal, and Finance. Externally, you’ll work closely with partners’ risk and compliance teams, including senior management.

Responsibilities

  • Lead risk-focused initiatives with global financial partners, including banks, networks, and payment methods, to support new business opportunities and user verticals, develop shared risk methodologies, and establish and maintain compliance with agreed risk appetites
  • Manage relationships with key risk counterparts at partner banks and develop projects and initiatives that support those relationships
  • Deliver business and policy recommendations that inform Stripe’s risk posture
  • Represent and negotiate Stripe’s risk approach with banking partners
  • Improve existing partner-facing risk management capabilities and develop new ones
  • Lead risk-related partnership and product discussions with banking partners to align on risk approaches and strategies
  • Identify and pursue business opportunities by creating risk-aware solutions that expand Stripe’s product and user base through banking partnerships

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in a risk-related role at a bank or merchant acquirer, or a role requiring deep knowledge of risk and compliance issues; 5+ years of experience in risk management at a bank or merchant acquirer
  • Ability to represent Stripe on risk, compliance, and product issues with banking partners to maintain positive relationships
  • Strong organizational, planning, and written and verbal communication skills to support understanding, collaboration, and issue resolution
  • 2+ years of experience improving processes and scaling solutions
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, including handling difficult situations, negotiating timelines, and influencing stakeholders across organizations and borders, along with the ability to work proactively and independently in uncertain and ambiguous environments

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with financial crime programs, including know your customer and know your business processes, anti-money laundering, sanctions, and counter-terrorist financing, with practical knowledge of the Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering regulations
  • Strong understanding of the complex risks involved in managing a merchant acquiring business, including high-risk sectors
  • Market experience across America and Canada, with an understanding of how current and future regulations will affect Stripe and its banking partners
  • Experience using technology to develop and embed scalable risk and operational processes

jobs.description:

Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions

We are seeking an experienced compliance leader to serve as Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) for Coinbase's Abu Dhabi-based subsidiary. This is a founding role within our Compliance organization: you will build the AML/CTF/PF/Sanctions compliance program in a high-growth market and directly shape our regulatory strategy with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM), balancing compliance with innovation. You will own all aspects of the entity's Anti-Money Laundering program, manage its relationship with the FSRA for AML/CTF purposes, and advise business and product teams on local requirements. The role is supported by Coinbase's global compliance infrastructure.

What you'll do:

  • Own identification of AML/CTF/PF and Sanctions requirements applicable to the ADGM entity, maintain policies and procedures as regulatory and business requirements evolve, and ensure ongoing compliance.
  • Monitor FSRA and UAE regulatory developments and lead implementation of necessary compliance changes with internal stakeholders.
  • Provide regular updates to senior management and the entity's Board on the AML/CTF/PF/Sanctions program, escalating incidents and material issues promptly, and drive AML/CTF/PF training for local employees and Board members.
  • Lead day-to-day regulatory communications with the FSRA, including notifications and comment letters, and oversee AML/CTF/PF risk assessments to confirm the adequacy of systems and controls.
  • Own timely remediation of findings from internal audit, regulatory exams, and self-identified issues.
  • Partner with Compliance and Product stakeholders to embed compliance into new products and market expansions, and with global teams to keep the AML/CTF/PF control environment consistent and integrated.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of AML/CTF/PF compliance experience, including senior leadership roles.

SKILLS YOU’LL NEED TO BRING - Frontline management experience leading customer-facing GTM teams in B2B software, ideally across Customer Success, Solutions Consulting, Technical Account Management, Professional Services, Account Management, or post-sales strategy. - Direct experience coaching teams through customer discovery, workflow design, adoption planning, value realization, renewals, expansion, or technical/workflow implementation. - Strong coaching orientation: you can review a customer call, account plan, mutual success plan, or executive value narrative and identify specifically what needs to change — not just whether the outcome was good, but why and how to improve it. - Commercial instincts at the team level: able to read account health, renewal risk, adoption depth, expansion potential, and customer sentiment, then drive urgency without micromanaging every account. - Deep customer-facing discovery instincts, with the ability to understand business problems, map workflows, and translate goals into practical adoption and implementation plans. - Experience operating in a shared account ownership model with Sales, Solution

テクニカルアカウントマネージャー (Technical Account Manager)

Asanaのテクニカルアカウントマネジャー（Technical Account Manager: TAM）は、顧客が日々の業務において「明瞭さ（Clarity）」を見出し、Asanaを活用して成果を上げることを支援します。TAMはAsanaのエキスパートであり、顧客の成功に情熱を注ぐ生産性のプロフェッショナルです。顧客からの質問、機能リクエスト、インシデント報告に対応し、中長期的な視点でのAsana活用のためのベストプラクティスを提供します。また、Asana社内では顧客の声を製品開発に反映させるための代弁者となり、製品開発チームと対話します。TAMの成功指標は「顧客の成功」であり、顧客への深い共感（Empathy）を通じてそれを実現します。

AsanaのTAMとして、あなたは大規模かつ複雑な要件を持つエンタープライズ顧客に対し、戦略的な技術アドバイザーとしてサポートを提供します。顧客のステークホルダーと深く連携し、技術的なイネーブルメント（定着化）を推進し、継続的な利用を確実にするとともに、Asanaの機能を顧客の長期的目標に合致させます。この役割は、強力な技術的適性、卓越した顧客への共感力、そして社内外のステークホルダーを巻き込む影響力が求められる、クロスファンクショナルなポジションです。

【勤務地・働き方】

このポジションはAsana Japanの技術本部長にレポートします。

私たちは、居住地に関わらず最適な人材をお迎えしたいと考えています。そのため、ご本人の状況に合わせて以下のいずれかの働き方を用意しています。

  • 関東圏にお住まいの方： 東京オフィスを拠点とした、オフィス中心のハイブリッドスケジュール（原則 月・火・木曜出社）となります。

  • 関東圏以外にお住まいの方（日本国内）： リモートワークでの勤務が可能です。ただし、チームビルディングや重要会議のため、月1〜2回程度、東京オフィスへの出社をお願いしています（詳細は面接時にご案内します）。

なお、重要な会議やオンサイト支援など、状況に応じて顧客先への訪問や国内出張が発生する場合があります。

【主な業務内容】

  • 顧客への技術的アドバイザリーとベストプラクティスの提供

  • エンタープライズ顧客の導入後における「技術的な成功（Technical Success）」に責任を持ち、Asana活用拡大の主要な技術アドバイザーおよびパートナーとして機能する。

  • Asana API、サードパーティサービスとの連携、認証（SAML/SCIM）、クラウドセキュリティおよび管理者ガバナンスに関するベストプラクティスを、顧客の環境や目標に合わせて設計・提案する。

  • 顧客のシステムアーキテクチャ、ビジネス上の優先順位、技術構成に関する深い知識を維持し、ニーズを先読みした提案を行う。

  • 顧客の健全性維持とリスク管理

  • 顧客との定期的なコミュニケーションや技術レビューを通じて顧客におけるAsana利活用にプロアクティブに関与し、製品価値の定着と継続的な利用を促進する。

  • セールス、カスタマーサクセスマネージャ（CSM）と共同で利用パターンやエンゲージメント傾向からヘルススコアを監視し、リスクの早期発見や、利用拡大・再エンゲージメントの機会を特定する。

  • 各種エスカレーション、移行プロジェクト、重大インシデント対応を社内各部門と連携して主導し、予防・早期検知・透明性のあるコミュニケーションを通じてリスクを最小化する。

  • 社内連携と製品へのフィードバック

  • 社内の技術ナレッジの標準化を推進し、再現性のあるベストプラクティスを策定・共有することで、チーム全体の提案力向上に貢献する。

  • セールス、サポート、プロダクト、エンジニアリングチームと緊密に連携し、統一された顧客体験を提供する。

  • 顧客の声を代弁し、実際のユースケースや課題に基づいたフィードバックを行うことで、製品ロードマップへ影響を与える。

【応募資格】

  • 経験とドメイン知識

  • SaaS業界における、顧客対面型の技術的役割（TAM、ソリューションエンジニア、導入コンサルタントなど）での5年以上の経験。

  • ワークフロー、自動化、ビジネスプロセス管理（BPM）など、業務プロセスに関わるSaaS・ソフトウェアを直接取り扱った経験。

  • ※インフラやセキュリティ領域専業ではなく、ビジネスロジックやアプリケーション層の課題解決に関わった経験を重視します。

  • 大規模なエンタープライズ顧客の複雑なステークホルダー管理を行い、プロジェクトを成功に導いた実績。

  • 技術的専門性

  • API、システム連携、認証プロトコル（SAML, SCIM）、および技術アーキテクチャについて、顧客と自信を持って議論できる技術的知見。

  • SaaSインフラ、セキュリティ基準、エンタープライズIT環境に関する広範な理解。

  • 顧客の技術的な課題や質問を素早く理解し、複雑な概念を噛み砕いて解決策を提示する能力。

  • コミュニケーションと言語能力

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

We’re moving fast, reinventing playbooks, and actively embracing the new era of AI and modern organizational dynamics. We operate with a creative, problem-solving mindset that prioritizes common-sense solutions and business-focused metrics. If you thrive on building trusted leader relationships, tackling complex talent challenges, and driving measurable impact, this is the team for you.

This role is open to candidates residing in the US or Canada.

jobs.title: Head of KYC
jobs.description:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions

As the Senior Manager, Head of KYC within Central Compliance, you'll own the global strategy, policy, and program execution for KYC across all Coinbase regulated entities. The KYC function operates as a shared services model, providing compliance advisory to Coinbase's global business lines. You'll serve as Coinbase's subject matter expert and senior escalation point for KYC, driving program design across jurisdictions, managing a team of KYC professionals, and partnering with operations, business, product, and regulatory stakeholders to ensure Coinbase's KYC program scales with the business while meeting evolving global regulatory requirements.  

What you’ll do: 

  • Own the end-to-end strategic direction of Coinbase's Global KYC program, including policy development, program implementation, advisory support, and enterprise-wide process design across all regulated entities.
  • Lead a team of KYC professionals across second-line compliance supporting program design, setting performance standards, developing talent, and ensuring consistent execution across jurisdictions.
  • Drive KYC issue management and resolution globally, providing oversight of corrective actions, systemic enhancements, and first-line KYC function performance.
  • Partner with sales, coverage, account management, customer experience, product, and engineering teams to design and implement KYC initiatives for new product and jurisdiction launches.
  • Serve as the Directly Responsible Individual (DRI) for regulatory reporting and correspondence related to global KYC program inquiries, and deliver senior management and executive-level reporting on KPIs and program health.
  • Shape the interpretation and implementation of global KYC requirements in collaboration with Legal and Compliance colleagues and business stakeholders, designing scalable solutions that balance regulatory compliance with business velocity. 

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 10+ years of experience managing, designing, and implementing KYC programs at a financial institution, including direct people management experience, preferably with digital assets and/or fintech exposure.
  • Deep knowledge of global AML, CTF, and sanctions regulations (e.g., BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, FinCEN CDD Rule, 4MLD/5MLD/6MLD, OFAC sanctions) and demonstrated ability to translate regulatory requirements into scalable KYC program design across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling a global KYC program from design through execution, including policy development, risk-based frameworks, and operational process implementation.
  • Experience serving as a senior escalation point for KYC/onboarding matters, with the ability to advise on client risk, provide regulatory guidance to cross-functional teams, and represent the KYC function to regulators and senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage concurrent regulatory initiatives, jurisdiction launches, and program enhancements in a matrixed environment while delivering executive-level reporting on program performance.
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)). 

 

Annual base salary range (excluding equity and bonus):
$252,620—$297,200 USD

We’re looking for a Senior Systems Analyst, Enterprise Apps (Finance) to join our Enterprise Applications and Architecture team. The mission of our team is to drive automation through an integrated suite of enterprise systems and technologies, streamlining the business operations and freeing up our finance team’s time to focus on high-judgment tasks. In this role, you will serve as our financial systems subject matter expert primarily supporting Zip,  Netsuite and other financial technologies. You will partner with our product managers and sourcing, legal, accounting, security team members to translate business requirements into technical solutions that can scale and support the growth of the company. You will join a small, agile and a tight-knit engineering team that is focussed on delivering value. We are seeking individuals who love problem solving and thrive in a continuous-learning and high level-of-ownership environment.

What you’ll be doing (ie. job duties): To be completed by all business teams except Eng.

  • Partner with Product Managers and finance stakeholders to implement the product roadmap for Zip, Navan, NetSuite and other financial applications.
  • Analyze current business processes, perform fit/gap analysis and translate the business requirements into technical solutions. 
  • Demonstrate knowledge of Zip’s capabilities for key processes: Source to Pay, Order to Cash, General Accounting and Financial Reporting.
  • Perform platform administration, maintenance and support on a day to day basis for Zip and boundary systems. 
  • Create engineering artifacts -  Functional and Technical Specifications, Data Flow Diagrams and Business Architecture Diagrams.
  • Design and build scalable solutions in Zip and other applications, including customizations, workflows, integrations and analytics/reporting.
  • Collaborate with citizen developers and engineers across multiple teams to develop and implement AI automations and agentic flows. 
  • Develop and execute test plans for identified  features, lead  integration and user acceptance testing with cross-functional teams. 
  • Participate in all engineering maturity activities (Agile, Observability, TechDebt Management, Automated Testing, Incident and Defect Management).
  • Troubleshoot and fix production issues, prioritizing them against the existing backlog based on severity and impact.
  • Support the business process transformation initiatives to improve efficiencies around critical activities like Month End Closure and Reporting.
  • Conduct solution walkthroughs, application demos and user training sessions.

What we look for in you (ie. job requirements): To be completed by all business teams except Eng. 

  • 5+ years of system administration  experience of Source to Pay systems like Zip,Coupa,  NetSuite and other finance applications like Navan, Brex, Oracle.
  • 4+ years of hands-on configuration experience  of various Zip  modules - Vendor Management, Sourcing Intake, Procurement, Payables, Payment, Taxes, Customizations (custom forms, fields, roles, queues),  Workflows, AI Agents (native and custom agents) and Reporting.
  • 3+ years of experience with large scale implementations of Sourcing/Procurement systems and their integrations through middleware technologies like Zip AppStudio/Workato/MulseSoft/Boomi.
  • 1+ years of experience with AI technologies - designing, building and deploying slackbots and/or workflow-based agents using n8n and Workato Genie.
  • Strong understanding of system-to-system integration principles, data flow patterns, and enterprise integration technologies, including web services, REST/SOAP APIs, file-based integrations, event-driven architectures, and MCP-based connectivity.
  • Strong knowledge of finance related business processes such as Sourcing, Procurement, Payables, Vend

jobs.title: Customer Activation Manager | Mid-Market
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp's Mid-Market Customer Activation Managers don't manage accounts — they transform how companies run their finances. This is a role for people who have been inside organizations when change was hard, who speak the language of a CFO, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll own a book of ~45 mid-market customers, responsible for driving genuine workflow transformation — not just onboarding completion What You'll do 1. Lead mid-market customers through the full transformation journey — from implementation through agentic workflow adoption — with clear accountability for time-to-value and measurable business outcomes 2. Build and own the change management strategy for each account: map stakeholders, diagnose resistance, build internal coalitions, and drive adoption past the finish line 3. Quantify and communicate Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about — close cycle improvement, spend visibility, variance reduction, and ROI — not just product usage metric 4. Run stakeholder management across multiple layers of a customer org, including finance leadership relationships you own independently 5. Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match 6. Help customers understand and adopt Ramp's agentic finance capabilities — positioning new workflows not as features, but as fundamental changes to how their finance team operates 7. Partner with Account Executives and Technical Consulting to deliver seamless implementations and expand Ramp's footprint within accounts 8. Bring customer insight back to Product — surfacing patterns, gaps, and opportunities from your accounts to shape how Ramp evolves What You'll Need - 5+ years of customer-facing experience in customer success, consulting, or implementations with a proven, consistent track record of driving customer outcomes and exceeding goals - Demonstrated ability to drive workflow adoption inside organizations, navigate real resistance from real stakeholders, and produce measurable results; finance or fintech context is a plus but not required - AI fluency as a daily habit — you already use AI tools habitually to prep for calls, synthesize information, build customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks; this is how you work, not something you're exploring - Ability to communicate Ramp's impact in financial terms — walking a controller through the business case for a workflow change, connecting implementation milestones to P&L outcomes, and running executive updates that land with finance leaders - Technical acumen to hold your own in conversations with Product and Engineering on integrations, APIs, and workflow architecture; credibility in technical conversations earns you a seat at the table with the full customer stakeholder group - Prior demonstrated success in fast-paced, results-oriented GTM environments, ideally at SaaS or FinTech companies - Strong collaboration and influencing skills across Sales, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams Nice to Haves 1. Experience helping customers adopt AI-powered or agentic workflows at scale; understanding of what friction looks like in practice and what makes transformation stick 2. Exposure to FP&A, accounting software ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, Xero), expense management, or CFO-adjacent workflows 3. Demonstrated commercial impact — expansion, retention, or time-to-value outcomes with specific metrics attached 4. Background at an AI-first or AI transformation company where rethinking workflows around AI was part of the product or culture 5. Management consulting background with structured problem-solving, client management, and the ability to turn ambiguity into a plan 6. High-growth or startup experience with comfort operating in ambiguity and rapid change For candidates located in NYC or SF, the pay range for this role is $128,000 -

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

Foundation Insights & Operations (I&O) enables leaders across People, Finance, and Legal & Compliance to move from strategy to execution. We lead high-impact, cross-functional programs, build scalable operating systems, and incubate new capabilities, including AI-native workflows. We are strategic operators, not coordinators: we help frame ambiguous problems, build reusable playbooks, and leave teams stronger than we found them.

As an Insights & Operations partner, you'll be strategically aligned to POST, our people technology, HRIS, People Systems Engineering, recruiting operations, and Global Ops teams. POST builds products for employees, and you'll help it operate like a true product org: roadmapping, supporting build prioritization, streamlining how work gets built, and landing launches well with the Gusties who use them. You'll also own comms strategy for POST's employee-facing work, planning what employees hear, from whom, and when, so launches and changes land clearly and not as surprises.

About the Team:

Foundation I&O is a small, high-leverage team that partners with Foundation leaders across People, Finance, and Legal & Compliance. We organize around programs (for example environment and community, employee relations and People Partner programs, total rewards, and POST) so each person builds real depth, and we build playbooks and operating mechanisms that outlast any single project.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Maintain the POST roadmap and surface dependencies and tradeoffs
  • Support prioritization conversations with POST leaders by bringing evidence and clear recommendations, without owning the backlog
  • Design and improve intake, planning cadences, and launch checklists
  • Own comms strategy for POST launches and changes, covering audience, sequencing, channels, and timing, in partnership with People Comms and POST leaders
  • Plan launch and adoption work, and report on portfolio status and patterns to People leadership

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 5+ years of People, technology, or operations program or product management experience, including 2+ years driving multi-stakeholder, cross-functional programs end to end
  • Experience with roadmapping and prioritization, ideally for internal or employee-facing technology
  • Experience planning and sequencing communications for employee-facing launches or organizational change
  • A track record of building processes, playbooks, or program infrastructure that teams adopted
  • Comfort working with technical teams and translating between engineering, People, and business partners
  • Strong written communication, including audience-based messaging for employees, managers, and leaders
  • Hands-on use of AI tools in your daily work to speed up synthesis, drafting, and documentation
  • Genuine interest in employee-facing work; prior People team experience is not required
  • Preferred: HRIS or People technology experience (such as Workday), and experience leading change management and adoption for employee-facing launches

Our cash compensation amount for this role is $127,660/yr to $157,447/yr in Denver & most major metro locations, and $154,895/yr to $191,037/yr for San Francisco & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management (Consumer)
jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Product team 

The Product team listens to our customers’ needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision.

About the role

Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without hidden fees or compounding interest. Our Direct to Consumer Products, Surfaces, and Growth programs are a fast-growing product set that operates with the agility of a startup while leveraging the scale of an industry leader, delivering quality Consumer Experiences to our Consumers and Growth to the business alike.

You will be a pivotal strategic leader responsible for defining the next chapter of Affirm's Consumer & Card Growth programs. You will lead a portfolio of high-impact consumer journeys that directly influence conversion, engagement, and revenue. This is a role for a seasoned product leader obsessed with consumer experiences and quality, driving Consumer Product growth ie Cards, and disrupting the payments & credit landscape

What you'll do

  • Strategic Leadership: Define and socialize a long-term Growth and App vision and strategy, and translate that vision into clear roadmaps and decisions that teams can execute against
  • Portfolio Oversight: Manage and scale a portfolio of consumer-facing surfaces, and growth platforms, including Onboarding flows, App surfaces, and platforms like Segmentation & Targeting services, ensuring a simple and consistent experience across platforms
  • Lead and grow a high-performing PM team. Build, mentor, and manage a team of product managers, including people managers. You'll set the bar for craft, create development paths, and cultivate a culture of ownership, rigor, and candor.
  • Executive Communication: Proactively align senior leadership on strategy, execution risks, and mitigation plans, ensuring organizational clarity during complex initiatives
  • Drive cross-functional alignment at scale: Partner with Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Revenue leaders to optimize the marketplace ecosystem, balancing merchant value with consumer experiences
  • Operational Excellence: Establish frameworks for rigorous experimentation and funnel analysis to drive measurable gains in completion rates and customer retention

What we look for

  • Experience: 10+ years of product management leadership, with a proven track record of shipping large-scale consumer products in fintech, e-commerce, or marketplace environments.
  • Strategic Clarity: Demonstrated ability to bring "clarity when things feel messy," turning ambiguous problems into crisp narratives and structured execution plans.
  • AI/LLM Fluency: Familiarity with AI-native product development, including agentic patterns and LLM-powered discovery experiences, to lead our highest-leverage bets in search
  • Analytical Rigor: Exceptional ability to use data (including LTV/CAC and profitability assessments) to guide prioritization and quantify the impact of product features.
  • People Leadership: Experience operating through layers of leadership, delegating ownership effectively, and scaling decision-making across diverse product lines.
  • Consumer Empathy: A "consumer-first" mindset with a high bar for design polish and a commitment to delivering honest financial products

Pay Grade - T
Equity Grade - USA 18

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)

USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $300,000 - $360,000
USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $267,000 - $327,000

As Scale AI continues its historic growth trajectory in Generative AI, we are seeking a Growth Strategy & Operations Lead to help ensure our customer projects have the expert capacity they need to deliver on time. You Have

  • A track record of influencing enterprise-wide compliance programs and advising executive leadership on complex matters
  • Strong knowledge of compliance regulations, risks, and typologies, paired with an analytical, metrics-driven approach to building substantiated solutions

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

We're excited about you because you have…

jobs.description:
About the Team

New Verticals is an exciting team at DoorDash that is building and scaling new ways to delight our customers beyond restaurant delivery.

Our Central Operations team, part of New Verticals Strategy & Operations, is re-inventing how consumers shop grocery, convenience, alcohol and retail by making every store’s digital shelf match the physical shelf. We do this by onboarding new data sources that improve selection coverage, price accuracy, inventory accuracy, and the location data that helps Dashers find the store and the item. When these get better, consumers see what they want at the right price and receive it with fewer substitutions and refunds, Dashers shop and navigate faster, and merchants sell more. You will partner with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to build AI-enabled tooling, launch operational processes at scale, own metrics, and pull operational and product levers across our Grocery, Convenience, Alcohol and Retail businesses.

About the Role

We are looking to hire a Manager to own how we onboard new data sources, external and internal, onto our ecosystem. Externally, you will bring on inventory and syndicated data providers, CPG branded data, in-store robotics companies, and other software and technology partners. Internally, you will find new ways to leverage the data we already have. Together, these sources align the physical inventory of brick-and-mortar stores with the digital inventory. You will also explore how these assets could grow into an inventory-as-a-service solution. You will partner with Machine Learning, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and Commercial teams. You will sit in the Central Operations group within our New Verticals Strategy & Operations organization and report into a Senior Manager. You will manage a team of two.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Build from zero. You’ll take new data sources from ideation to production: sizing opportunities, structuring partnerships, running pilots, and scaling the winners across Convenience, Grocery, Alcohol, and Retail.
  • Think big. You’ll imagine what’s possible with new sources and new commercial models, including inventory as a service, and turn bold ideas into roadmaps.
  • Close the physical-digital gap. You’ll connect real-world signals from retailers, syndicated data, CPGs, robots, and software partners to improve selection coverage, price accuracy, inventory accuracy, and Dasher navigation.
  • Own the economics. You’ll define the commercial and business metrics that show when a source works and when it doesn’t, and weigh the lift against the cost to make clear scale, iterate, or stop decisions.
  • Lead. You’ll partner with Engineers, Data Scientists, Product Managers, and Commercial teams to integrate sources and drive measurable impact.

We’re excited about you because…

  • You think 0 to 1. You’re energized by ambiguity, think boldly and unconstrained about what new sources could unlock, and resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
  • You’re creative about business models. You can see how data becomes a product, and help shape the strategy behind it.
  • You understand the interplay of commercial and business metrics. You know how selection, price, and inventory accuracy translate into conversion, retention, and cost, and you can tell when a data source is worth what it costs.
  • You’re analytical. You can extract and communicate meaningful insights from data to drive strategic decisions, and you are comfortable with SQL and data visualization tools.
  • You’re an operator and a partner. You’re comfortable in the details of data quality and store-level operations, and you can build and negotiate relationships with external vendors, CPGs, and technology companies.
  • You have 6-8+ years of experience. You’ve succeeded in high-performing cultures (tech, supply chain, operations, strategy, business development, consulting, banking, startups or a related experience), ideally with data

Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. You'll manage deal execution across the pipeline, build relationships with partner stakeholders, and contribute market insights that shape how Coinbase positions its infrastructure products to financial institutions.

  • Originate new partnership opportunities with PSPs, fintechs, and banks by researching high-potential prospects and developing tailored outreach and engagement strategies.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. This role is designed for someone who brings deep procurement domain expertise, technical implementation knowledge, and architect-level solution design skills to accelerate Ramp’s most complex, high-value enterprise evaluations. You will support enterprise Account Executives and Solutions Consultants in running sophisticated procurement cycles end-to-end — leading deep discovery, validating technical requirements, designing future-state workflows, and creating pre-sale implementation plans that ensure a seamless handoff to onboarding. Build pre-sale implementation plans (phases, timelines, dependencies) to eliminate re-discovery during onboarding - Conduct integration assessments, including API workflow validation, SFTP/data exchange requirements, and security/permissions modeling - Create workflow prototypes, configurations, and proof-of-concepts when needed to accelerate technical validation PARTNER WITH SALES TO WIN COMPLEX ENTERPRISE DEALS - Operate as the procurement technical lead in enterprise opportunities - Join high-value and complex P2P evaluations as the primary procurement SME, either as an overlay or as the lead SC for procurement-first deals - Quantify customer pain, run gap analyses, and translate procurement challenges into measurable ROI and value propositions INFLUENCE PRODUCT AND GTM STRATEGY - Provide structured feedback to Product on gaps, customer needs, and market trends - Help shape Ramp’s procurement roadmap and competitive positioning - Maintain a bird’s-eye view of the procurement technology landscape to inform strategic decisions ENSURE SEAMLESS HANDOFF TO ONBOARDING - Document all procurement requirements, decisions, and implementation guidance in a standardized format - Partner closely with Implementation and Technical Consulting teams to ensure they begin activation without additional discovery - Maintain consultative availability throughout onboarding when complex escalations arise TRAVEL - Travel up to 30%+ for onsite discovery workshops, executive briefings, and solution validation sessions WHAT YOU NEED - 8+ years of experience in Procurement, P2P, ERP, or similar technical implementation roles - Deep understanding of end-to-end procurement processes, including sourcing, procurement operations, vendor management, AP, bill pay, and contract workflows - Hands-on experience designing or implementing P2P solutions (Coupa, Ariba, Zip, Ivalua, Workday, NetSuite, etc.) - Strong technical acumen — API experience required, plus familiarity with SFTP, integrations, data migration, SCIM/SAML, and ERP financial objects - Experience running enterprise evaluations with C-suite and VP-level stakeholders - Exceptional communication and storytelling skills with the ability to translate complex workflows into clear solutions - Ability to design future-state workflows and build pre-sale implementation plans NICE TO HAVE - Certifications in Coupa, Ariba

jobs.description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role

This is a highly customer-facing role at the intersection of engineering, solution architecture, agentic AI, and customer delivery. You will work directly with stakeholders and own the technical discovery for our ongoing opportunities end to end. Once a deal is qualified, you scope, build, embed with the client, and build it yourself, code that holds up against real tax and jurisdiction data, not a prototype you clean up later. What you ship only counts once the client is paying for it, it's live, and it's measurably cutting the manual work they used to do by hand, hours saved, tickets deflected, risk reduced. You should be comfortable speaking with both technical and executive stakeholders, moving quickly from problem discovery to prototype, and turning complex workflows into production-ready agents and multi-agent systems.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day

  • Scope & Qualify: Give Sales a technical feasibility read early on ambiguous Enterprise opportunities, then own scoping the compliance challenge once the deal is sales-qualified.
  • Define the Problem: Own requirements gathering on complex, ambiguous opportunities, scoping the problem clearly enough for Sales, Product, and Engineering to align on it.
  • Prove It First: Build a working proof-of-concept of the proposed agent when a deal needs to see feasibility before committing to the full build, tailored from a hands-on integration engineer to a VP of Payroll Tax.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technical Brand & Content
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Airbnb’s mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we work to achieve that mission, our cross functional Tech Operations and Programs team helps enable Tech organizations to execute and deliver on high impact programs and initiatives. 

The Difference You Will Make:

You will decide what the engineering world knows about Airbnb.

  • Our engineers solve hard problems at scale across infrastructure, data, and applied AI — and they write about that work well. Almost none of the engineers we'd most like to hire have ever seen it.
  • You'll change that, and the change is measurable. A year in, senior candidates should arrive already able to describe our technical work accurately, because they found it before we found them. Our engineers should be recognised names in their fields rather than anonymous authors. Airbnb should be the source people cite on at least one technical domain. And the strongest engineers in the market should have a reason to choose us that has nothing to do with the offer.
  • That is a rare kind of impact for this discipline. Most tech brand roles are asked to manufacture credibility that isn't there. Here the engineering is genuinely strong and already documented — the gap is that it doesn't travel. You'd be building the function that closes it, with real autonomy, very little inherited process, and direct access to engineering leaders and our CTO.

A Typical Day:

  • Own the editorial engine. Run the Airbnb Tech Blog end to end: sourcing topics from teams, coaching engineer-authors, editing to a high bar, and moving posts through legal, security and comms review without letting them stall. Set and hold a publishing rhythm the org can rely on.
  • Find the cross-team narratives. Our biggest gap is that individually strong posts never add up to a story. You'll work across orgs to identify the themes that connect work from multiple teams, and publish them as connected sets — while each domain keeps publishing in depth for its own specialists.
  • Build our voices. Help our engineers and technical leaders develop genuine public presence: bylines, talks, speaker coaching, and a pipeline of new voices. This includes partnering closely with our CTO to establish his public technical presence.
  • Own distribution. Establish our canonical home on an Airbnb-owned domain, stand up the surfaces we're missing including video, and decide what our social channels are for. Publishing well and distributing poorly is the pattern we're here to break.
  • Run our external presence. Set conference and event strategy — where we speak, where we sponsor, where we skip — and manage what we host ourselves. Own our academic collaborations and technical media relationships, and the budget and vendors behind all of it.
  • Steward our open source presence. Make sure what Airbnb claims publicly is accurate and actually maintained, and that the projects carrying our name reflect how we want to be seen.
  • Prove it works. Partner with Talent Acquisition to connect this work to hiring outcomes — inbound share of the senior pipeline, offer acceptance at staff level and above in ML and infrastructure — and be honest about what is and isn't attributable.

Your Expertise:

  • Substantial experience in technical content, developer relations, engineering communications or technical editorial — including time spent working directly with engineers, not adjacent to them.
  • Technical fluency. You don't need to write production code, but you need to hold your own in a systems design conversation, read a design doc, and judge whether a draft post says anything real. Credibility with staff engineers is the difference between this role working and not working.
  • Editorial judgment and hands-on craft. You can edit an engineer's draft into something sharper without flattening their voice, and you know the difference between a post that teaches something and one that announces something.
  • Influence without authority. Nothing you need is owned by you. You've built systems and incentives that got busy senior people to produce, rather than relying on persistence.
  • Program discipline. You've owned events, budgets and vendors end to end, and you're comfortable with the unglamorous half of the job.

We’re seeking an experienced security leader to lead Affirm’s global security investigations and incident response program as we expand internationally. This leader will guide complex investigations and incidents while building the operating practices, readiness, and technical capabilities needed to support consistent response across regions and scale with the business.

In this role, you’ll lead a technically deep, engineering-oriented team that manages major incidents and builds better response capabilities. You’ll direct complex investigations while staying close to the technical work, bring structure to ambiguity, guide responders and executives through critical decisions, and turn incident findings into durable engineering improvements. jobs.description:
About the Team

The Dasher & Logistics team supports the millions of Dashers who power DoorDash's marketplace. Dasher Financial is our bet that the financial system serving gig workers should be built by the platform they already work on. From instant access to earnings, to bill pay and savings, to credit-building tools, our goal is to become the financial home for Dashers. Our banking product serves 2M+ monthly active Dashers, and the business has more than doubled in the past year.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Manager to run our banking business, and to grow into the GM of it. This is a business already at scale: millions of users, it generates real revenue, and it runs on a regulated program with a sponsor bank and processor partners. But the business is also early enough that the decisions you make will help determine what this becomes.

The first twelve months are about making the business stronger on every axis at once: growing the user base and the revenue levers that already work, taking down the cost to serve, and pulling more of the banking operation under our own control. These three pull against each other, and deciding how to trade them off against the P&L is the job.

You'll also be the face of this business outside the company. Our processor, program manager, and sponsor bank determine what we can build, how fast, and at what cost. You'll own those relationships, hold partners to what they committed to, and sit at the table when we negotiate the next set of terms. This is a commercial role as much as an operational one.

And you'll lead the team that runs it, hiring and developing operators who own their surfaces while staying hands-on yourself. At this stage the person running the business is still personally in the data, in the partner rooms, and in the details of how the machine actually works.

You will:

  • Own the P&L - user growth, revenue per user, and cost to serve
  • Build the operating model for a regulated financial product: service levels, vendor accountability, escalation paths, and the controls that keep the program healthy
  • Own our external partnerships end to end and represent the business in negotiations
  • Find the next revenue levers in a business that already has scale, and make the case for what we should invest in
  • Develop and lead a team of operators, and build the bench that lets the business grow faster than headcount
  • Represent the business to DoorDash leadership as its owner

This seat is where that bet becomes a real business: a P&L you own, partners you negotiate with, and an operation you get to build. For someone who wants to run a company one day, it's the closest thing to doing it with a scaled platform behind you.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Run a business: own the P&L for a banking product millions of Dashers already use
  • Build the machine: design the operating model for a regulated financial product, and decide what we bring in-house, what we rent, and in what order.
  • Own external relationships: represent DoorDash with our sponsor bank and fintech partners
  • Find the next lever: identify where the next tranche of growth and revenue comes from in a business that already has scale, and make the case for the investment.
  • Lead people: develop operators who own their surfaces outright and build a team that grows the business faster than headcount
  • Grow into the GM seat: do the full job - strategy, P&L, operations, partners, and people - in a business early enough that your decisions still set its direction

We’re excited about you because…

  • You have 8+ years of experience, including time running something with real operational stakes - a business line, a large operational surface, or a P&L.
  • You take a vague, consequential problem and structure it yourself. 
  • You use data to make decisions, but you’re also comfortable taking a stance before the data proves you right.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's Connected Operations platform helps organizations that depend on physical operations — fleets, construction, utilities, public works, and first responders — run safer, more efficiently, and more sustainably. 

We're looking for a Principal Product Marketing Manager - Public Sector to own the narrative, positioning, and enablement that will define how Samsara wins in government. You'll be the team's expert on how public sector buyers evaluate technology — from the contract vehicles they procure through, to the compliance bar they hold vendors to, to the mission outcomes they're ultimately accountable for. 

This is a strategic, cross-functional role for someone who already understands government and frameworks like FedRAMP and StateRAMP/GovRAMP. The ideal candidate is someone who wants to build a public sector product marketing motion, not just execute inside one that already exists.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the U.S. We prefer candidates based in or near Washington, D.C., or those able to work Eastern time zone hours.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your work will have real-world stakes — helping public agencies keep roads plowed, fleets safe, and essential services running for the communities they serve.
  • You're fluent in how the government buys technology: You understand procurement cycles, contract vehicles, and compliance frameworks well enough to turn them into a go-to-market advantage rather than a blocker.
  • You're energized by building, not just executing: Samsara's federal go-to-market motion is still being defined — you'll have real ownership over the frameworks, positioning, and playbooks that shape it.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You'll be surrounded by a high-caliber team that pushes you to do your best work.

In this role, you will:

  • Own public sector positioning and messaging: Develop and evolve Samsara's core narrative for government buyers across federal, state, local, and education segments — grounded in mission outcomes rather than generic product benefits
  • Build Samsara's federal go-to-market foundation: Partner cross-functionally to define how Samsara approaches the federal market, including messaging and enablement that reflect our compliance roadmap as it evolves
  • Translate compliance into a sales advantage: Understand the FedRAMP authorization process and impact levels — deeply enough to explain it clearly to sales teams and prospects, and to inform internal conversations about authorization strategy and timing
  • Drive product and platform launches for public sector: Localize Samsara's launches for a government audience, ensuring messaging reflects agency use cases, procurement realities, and compliance considerations
  • Enable sales and channel teams: Build battlecards, objection-handling guides, RFP/RFI response content, and compliance-focused sales collateral that helps account teams and channel partners win competitive government deals

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

Submit your interest to join our Sales Onboarding Advocate team!

Gusto is seeking sales professionals who thrive in a fast-paced, consultative environment and are interested in being considered for future start dates in 2027. If you’d like to be considered for future opportunities with our team, please complete the form below and upload your resume. 

While start dates are still being determined for 2027, we’d love to connect! Does this sound like you? Apply below!

About the Role:

This role blends technical problem-solving with sales and customer service. After training, you'll be helping small business owners get their payroll and HR set up correctly. This means entering their past information, catching mistakes in their setup before they cause problems, and helping them navigate state and federal tax guidelines (every state does this differently, so you'll become the expert who can guide customers through all 50).

This team is where technical sales careers start at Gusto. You'll build a strong foundational understanding of payroll, tax, and compliance expertise while developing consultative sales skills, and that opens doors. Reps who excel here can grow into specialized roles working in Implementations and Solutions Engineering. If you're looking for a sales career with a technical backbone, this is where that path starts.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Customer conversations: Handle high-volume customer interactions across phone and email with small business owners guiding them from onboarding to running their first payroll.
  • Pipeline management: Own your ticket queue the way a seller owns their opportunity pipeline.

Operating across the entire customer and merchant lifecycle, we tackle a diverse array of challenges, from optimizing checkout conversion and mitigating fraud risk to building scalable data foundations and enabling international growth. We analyze performance not just to report on it, but to determine where to invest resources for maximum impact through building tools, scalable data infrastructure, and analytical frameworks.

We improve the analytics experience across Affirm by streamlining workflows and fostering a culture of learning and documentation. By taking ownership of the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision, we turn complex data and systems into clear, actionable signals that ensure Affirm grows efficiently and intelligently.

One Role, Multiple Teams

We are hiring multiple Senior Analyst roles across Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization through this single job posting. Rather than interviewing for one specific team, candidates will go through a shared interview process designed to assess the core skills we look for across R&A.

If selected, we will work with you to determine the best team match based on your interests, experience, strengths, and current business needs. You will have the opportunity to learn more about our teams and share your preferences as you move through the process.

Potential team placements include:

  • Point of Sale (POS): Optimize merchant and checkout performance to improve conversion, approvals, and unit economics across the purchase funnel.
  • Direct to Consumer (DTC) / Card: Drive engagement, repeat usage, and lifecycle health across Affirm's app, web, and card experiences.
  • Fraud: Prevent and reduce fraud losses across the customer journey while maintaining a frictionless user experience.
  • Core Analytics: Build the quantitative research, performance monitoring, and scalable data foundations that enable fast, economically sound decisions.
  • Servicing: Enhance the post-origination customer experience by analyzing repayment behavior, collections strategies, and operational efficiency.
  • International Expansion: Build the measurement and decision foundations needed to sustainably launch and scale Affirm in new global markets.

About the Role

As a Senior Analyst in Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization, you will join one of several analytical teams working across the customer and merchant lifecycle. While the specific problems you tackle will depend on your eventual team placement, all Senior Analyst roles share a common foundation: owning complex analytical problems end to end, translating data into business strategy, and influencing decisions across technical and non-technical teams.

You will operate with autonomy to own the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision. You bring exceptional analytical rigor, deep domain expertise, and the ability to translate complex regulatory, economic, and machine learning insights into actionable business strategies. You thrive in ambiguity, balance growth with resilience, and are comfortable operating at both strategic and execution levels to influence stakeholders across the organization.

What You Will Do

  • Optimize End-to-End Strategy: Leverage advanced data analytics to independently derive insights, develop, and optimize business, risk, or growth strategies across products and geographies.
  • Manage Macro & Market Trends: Monitor portfolio performance and exogenous macroeconomic trends, proactively adjusting analytical and operational strategies to mitigate risk and balance growth.
  • Model & Capability Building: Partner deeply with Engineering and Machine Learning teams to design, build, and interpret performance metrics for scalable risk, fraud, or growth models.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Collaborate closely with Product, Legal, and Compliance teams to interpret evolving regulatory and market requirements, translating them directly into analytical policy and product design recommendations.

jobs.description:
The Role

As the Head of Central Robot Operations, you will lead the central operations organization that powers autonomous robot delivery at scale. Acting as the operational command center for the business, you will build the capabilities, mechanisms, and teams that enable safe, reliable, and efficient robot operations across every market.

You will own the operating model spanning Remote Assistance, Mapping Operations, Market Expansion, Infrastructure, Strategy & Operations, Policy & Demos, and Program Management etc. This leader will establish the systems, governance, and operational excellence needed to scale autonomous operations from a handful of cities to a global network, partnering closely with Engineering, Product, Safety, Hardware, Autonomy, Legal, Public Policy, and Market Operations.

What You Will Do

Build and Scale Central Robot Operations

  • Define the long-term operating model, organizational structure, and roadmap for Central Robot Operations.
  • Build scalable mechanisms, operating standards, and governance that enable reliable robot operations across all markets.
  • Lead a high-performing organization spanning operations, analytics, expansion, mapping, infrastructure, and program management.

Own Remote Assistance Operations

  • Lead the 24/7 Remote Assistance organization responsible for supporting autonomous robots requiring human intervention.
  • Define response-time SLAs, workforce planning, staffing models, scheduling, and escalation protocols.
  • Develop monitoring, telemetry, and operational dashboards that provide real-time visibility into fleet health.
  • Partner with Engineering and Product to analyze intervention data, eliminate recurring failure modes, and continuously reduce human intervention rates.

Lead Mapping Operations

  • Own the operational lifecycle of geospatial assets including HD maps, geofences, routing data, and points of interest.
  • Establish mapping quality standards, QA mechanisms, refresh cycles, and operational readiness processes for new launches.
  • Balance mapping accuracy with launch velocity while managing internal and external mapping partners.

Drive Geographic Expansion

  • Develop the playbook for launching new cities, campuses, and operating zones.
  • Lead market assessment, regulatory readiness, operational planning, and launch governance.
  • Build repeatable launch mechanisms that enable rapid, high-quality expansion across multiple geographies.
  • Coordinate cross-functional readiness reviews prior to every market launch.

Own Market Infrastructure

  • Lead strategy and execution for hubs, depots, charging infrastructure, parking locations, maintenance facilities, and operational footprint.
  • Drive capacity planning, infrastructure utilization, vendor management, and cost optimization.
