jobs.description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you.

The Role

The best software companies don’t grow through direct sales alone. They grow through ecosystems: networks of partners who extend their reach, deepen customer relationships, and deliver outcomes no single company can achieve alone. Partner-engaged opportunities close at a significant multiple of the rate and deal size of direct-only deals, and Partner Sales Directors are essential to accelerating this model.

As Partner Sales Director, you own the direct partner sales motion across Enterprise and our Industry verticals (MEGS, FinServ, RCG): aligning Braze's Technology, Delivery, and Marketplace partners to the specific needs of the highest-value customers and prospects in your patch. These are the most complex accounts in the region, often involving GSIs and specialist SI partners, senior partner executives and exec sponsors on both sides. You report to the AVP, Partner Sales EMEA, set the partner strategy for your territory, and are often the person other Partner Sales Managers and Senior Partner Sales Managers in the region come to for guidance.

What You'll Own

  • Territory and account depth. Build and maintain a deep understanding of the customers and prospects within your territory - the partners already engaged on them, and the white space where a partner introduction would change the outcome. Crossbeam, Tackle, and Salesforce are your working tools.
  • Partner activation on live opportunities. Work alongside the Account Executives in your territory to get the right Delivery, Technology or Marketplace partner into the room early enough to matter, whether that's pipeline generation, competitive displacement, or a stalled deal that needs an outside push.
  • Customer value and retention. Partner with AMs and CSMs to identify where existing customers are underusing Braze, and bring in the partner who closes that gap, whether through implementation, a composable integration or ongoing managed services.
  • Joint Business Planning. Build and run the most complex, highest-stakes JBPs in the region with your priority partners, working closely with Partner Account Directors: shared targets, clear stakeholders, and a review cadence you hold everyone to.
  • Trusted advisor to Sales leadership. Be the person your Sales Director, AVP or VP Sales calls when they need a read on the partner landscape in your territory, and the person who proactively flags where a partner relationship is an asset or a risk on a specific deal.
  • Executive partner relationships. Build and hold relationships with partner executives and exec sponsors in your territory that go beyond a single deal, rooted in a genuine point of view on martech architecture and where composability creates value for the customer.
  • Coaching the field. Bring AEs up the curve on partner engagement: which partners are incumbent where, when to bring one in, and how to run that motion.
  • Ecosystem gaps and territory strategy. Identify where your territory is under-covered by partners and lead the work to close that gap, shaping the wider partner coverage strategy you feed back to the AVP and the Partnerships team.

Regional mentorship. Act as the go-to person for Partner Sales Managers and Senior Partner Sales Managers in your region, and represent the market in the AVP's absence when needed.

What This Role Is Really About

Pipeline sourced through partners is the outcome. The actual job is knowing your accounts so well, and your partner ecosystem so well, that connecting the two looks obvious in hindsight. That only happens through account mapping and relationship depth built over time, not through a partner directory or a marketing calendar.

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Recruiting at Brex

Recruiting is where every career at Brex begins. We are the first point of connection for future builders and leaders, helping candidates see what is possible. We partner with leaders across the company to find exceptional talent and build high-performing teams. We move quickly, think strategically, and take pride in a thoughtful, welcoming candidate experience from the first contact. We shape the culture at Brex by hiring the designers who define how our products look, feel and function.

What you'll do

Partner with product leaders to understand team needs and role requirements, and keep hiring goals aligned for Product roles. Source, engage and assess strong product talent through multiple channels, supporting the recruitment lifecycle from outreach to onboarding. Build pipelines for current openings and for upcoming hiring needs, with a focus on attracting diverse product talent. Track key hiring metrics, flag where candidates drop off, and help improve recruiting effectiveness. Work with the team to keep evaluation fair and consistent, and represent Brex in the product community, including events and social platforms.

Where you'll work

This role will be based in our San Francisco office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work.

Responsibilities

  • Lead sourcing and outreach for Product roles, using recruiting platforms, product communities and social networks.
  • Screen profiles for product sense, strategy and execution, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Work with product leaders to calibrate the product bar and hiring profile, with guidance from senior recruiters on strategy.
  • Schedule and coordinate interviews, including profile reviews and product case exercises, for a high-quality candidate experience.
  • Give hiring managers regular updates on pipeline health and progress.
  • Keep candidate data accurate and up to date in recruiting systems and dashboards.
  • Contribute ideas to improve recruiting processes, inclusive hiring and candidate experience.
  • Help promote Brex's employer brand in the product community.

Requirements

  • At least 2 years of experience recruiting or sourcing for technical roles ideally in-house, in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Solid sourcing skills and familiarity with AI tools, recruiting platforms and product talent networks.
  • Ability to review product profiles and understand product sense and how product teams work, and willingness to learn more.
  • Clear communication, relationship-building and stakeholder skills.
  • Comfort with recruiting data: reads basic metrics and suggests improvements.
  • Ability to manage several searches at once with guidance on priorities.

Bonus points

  • Experience recruiting product managers across Product, Growth or Platform.
  • Exposure to compensation and market data for product roles.
  • Interest or experience in employer branding for the product community.
  • Experience hiring across multiple geographies (US, Canada, LATAM).

Compensation

jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE Ramp is building new products that can reshape how finance teams operate. These products begin before the market playbook is obvious: the customer problem is still being sharpened, the product is evolving quickly, and the path from early signal to durable growth must be built. We are hiring a Product Marketing Manager, New Products to lead that work. You will be embedded with Product and Engineering from the earliest stages, using customer and market insight to help choose the audience, shape the product, define the story, and build the commercialization and adoption motion. This is not a launch-calendar or asset-production role. You will own the full business read for the product: customer problem, ICP, positioning, product readiness, launch, pipeline, activation, adoption, retention, proof, and the next product or GTM intervention. You'll be aligned to a product surface area based on business needs and your background. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Shape product strategy early. Bring customer, market, and competitive evidence into product decisions before the roadmap is fixed. Help the team identify the wedge, target segment, table stakes, differentiators, and highest-leverage problems to solve. - Find product-market clarity. Define the ICP, buyer, user, jobs to be done, workflow, alternatives, and reasons customers will switch or expand. - Own the product narrative. Build the canonical positioning, messaging, claims, proof, and competitive story. Translate technical and operational complexity into a clear customer value proposition without flattening how the product works. - Design the zero-to-one GTM. Determine how the product should enter the market, including audience, channel, pricing and packaging inputs, sales motion, self-serve motion, launch sequence, and adoption plan. - Lead launches end to end. Coordinate Product, Engineering, Sales, Growth, Creative, Communications, Support, and other partners around one launch strategy, readiness bar, and set of measurable outcomes. - Build commercialization, not just awareness. Create the programs, enablement, proof, and feedback loops that turn interest into qualified pipeline, activation, retained usage, expansion, and revenue. - Work deeply with Product and Engineering. Understand the product's architecture, data, constraints, and trust model well enough to influence tradeoffs and explain it credibly to both technical and business audiences. - Create the customer learning system. Develop direct relationships with buyers and users, run structured discovery, capture objections and product gaps, and turn what you learn into product and GTM decisions. - Own the business scorecard. Define leading and lagging indicators, build a clear operating read, diagnose what is moving or stuck, and recommend the next intervention. - Build proof and competitive intelligence. Develop customer evidence, use cases, benchmarks, and a current view of the market that improve both product decisions and GTM execution. - Use AI as an operating advantage. Apply AI to research, synthesis, analysis, content development, and repeatable workflows—and help the team raise its standard for speed and quality. - Create the new-products playbook. Build a repeatable method for taking an emerging product from customer signal to product-market clarity, launch, commercialization, and scaled growth. jobs.title: Solutions Engineer - French Speaker
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Solutions Engineer (SE) for France is a critical technical and business-driven consultant who understands the specific digital transformation needs of French and European enterprises. Acting as a trusted advisor, the SE provides business-centric expertise that helps our regional Sales team establish market relevance, secure deal-level visibility, and clearly differentiate Talkdesk's AI-powered solutions from legacy competitors.

This role is calibrated for a fully autonomous, mid-level operator who is highly "AI-savvy." You are not just a presenter of slides; you are a hands-on practitioner who knows how to configure conversational AI products, build live prototypes, and architect solutions. You will deeply understand the unique nuances of the French market—including data sovereignty expectations, regulatory compliance (such as GDPR), and complex system integrations—while maintaining fluent, daily collaboration in English with our global product and engineering teams.

Responsibilities

  • Hands-on AI Prototyping & Configuration: Design, build, and configure customized, live proof-of-concepts (PoCs) featuring Talkdesk Autopilot and AI Agents. This includes hands-on prompt engineering, defining Guardrails, setting up Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) knowledge sources, and mapping conversational flows.
  • Strategic French Market Advisory: Understand customer-specific business challenges in France and French-speaking Europe to provide consultative, business-driven solutions for prospective and existing customers, guiding them on how to transition from legacy, rigid IVRs to dynamic, AI-powered automation.
  • Deal Strategy & Differentiation: Partner with the regional Sales team to deliver business-centric expertise. Establish highly resonant, deal-level visibility that clearly positions Talkdesk's speed, agility, and AI superiority over competitor offerings.
  • Technical Architecture Design: Map out integrations between Talkdesk's AI suite and customer ecosystem technologies (CRMs, APIs, legacy telephony via SIP Trunking) to support seamless, secure automation.
  • End-to-End Sales Lifecycle Ownership: Smoothly transition across key facets of the sales cycle, including pre-sales engineering support, solution qualification, custom architecture design, and post-sale upsell strategy.
  • C-Suite Influence: Act as a credible thought leader confidently presenting to and addressing French C-level executives (CIOs, CTOs, COOs, and Customer Experience Directors) to expand revenue opportunities.

Requirements

  • Bilingual English & French Mastery: Native French speaker with professional business fluency in English. You must be equally comfortable leading a highly technical discovery call in French and jumping onto a global product call in English to discuss roadmap features, file bug reports, or write technical documentation.
  • AI & Prompt Engineering Savviness: Demonstrated experience configuring AI/NLP systems, LLM-based applications, or conversational AI platforms. You should understand how temperature, prompt design, and context windows affect AI agent performance.
  • High Responsiveness: Demonstrate an exceptional level of responsiveness to internal stakeholders and external clients throughout complex, fast-moving sales cycles.
  • Expert "Tell-Show-Tell" Presentation: Possess superior presentation and demonstration skills, both virtual and live, utilizing Talkdesk's "tell-show-tell" format to map technical features directly to tangible business value.

jobs.description:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. We’re remote-first by design and operate with intelligence at the center of everything we do. At Block, you'll be challenged by some of the brightest, most creative minds in the industry and have the tools and autonomy to do the most meaningful work of your career. 

The Role

This role puts you at the center of the team that independently challenges the models Square Financial Services relies on, from the credit models that decide who gets a loan to the forecasting models that shape the bank's plans. You'll help work out how to validate modeling approaches that are new to banking, often before an industry playbook exists. And with broad access to AI tools that few banks offer, you'll help rethink how validation itself gets done, so our team can run a rigorous program efficiently. If you enjoy digging into data and code, forming your own view of how a model really behaves, and explaining that view clearly to developers, leaders and bank examiners, this is the place to be.

As a Senior Model Risk Analyst, you will lead independent validations of models used across Square Financial Services (SFS), Block's bank, which lends to small businesses through Square Loans and to consumers through Cash App Borrow, and offers FDIC-insured deposits. Every SFS model must be independently reviewed and approved before it goes into use, so your work directly affects whether the bank can launch new products, grow lending and meet regulatory expectations safely and on time. You will report to the Head of AI & Model Risk and join the AI & Model Risk team, part of the bank's independent risk function. No two validations are alike: you will decide which tests matter for each model's data, methodology and intended use, with minimal day-to-day oversight.

You Will

  • Lead independent validations across the model lifecycle, scaling the depth of your work to each model's risk rating
  • Validate models used across the bank, including credit underwriting and loss forecasting models for small business and consumer lending, and finance models used for business planning, stress testing and balance sheet management
  • Evaluate conceptual soundness: methodology, data, assumptions, limitations and any management adjustments to model outputs
  • Verify that models work as intended: reproduce developer code (typically Python), test input data for accuracy and completeness with SQL, confirm outputs, and review evidence of accurate implementation, data integrity controls and security
  • Build independent benchmark or challenger models for high-risk models, and perform outcomes analysis such as backtesting and rank-ordering tests
  • Independently review each model owner's proposed risk rating and recommend a final rating
  • Assess ongoing monitoring plans and results, review vendor models and pre-approved model changes, and flag models that are deteriorating before they become a problem
  • Write clear validation reports, rate findings by severity, agree on remediation with model owners and track it to closure
  • Present your conclusions to model owners, senior management and the bank's risk committees, and support internal audits and FDIC examinations
  • Help keep the model inventory and validation records accurate, and build AI-enabled tools that make the validation program faster and more scalable

You Have

  • A minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as mathematics, statistics, data science, economics, finance or computer science; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience in model development, model validation or quantitative analysis
  • Hands-on experience developing or validating statistical and machine learning models, and in-depth knowledge of the quantitative methods used to test them
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, including working in and adapting code someone else wrote, plus familiarity with GitHub
  • Experience with one or more of these model types: credit underwriting, loss forecasting, stress testing, asset liability management or interest rate risk, or financial planning and forecasting
  • Strong technical writing, and the ability to explain complex model issues to non-technical partners, senior management and regulators
  • Sound judgment to scope a validation, choose the right tests and manage several validations at once

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Legal, Compliance, and Public Affairs team 

The Legal, Compliance, and Public Affairs team is a group of dedicated professionals committed to helping Affirm scale, innovate, and provide outstanding products for consumers, merchants, and key partners. We combine legal, compliance, and policy expertise to guide growth, shape products, and build trust across our ecosystem. Our work spans multiple professional disciplines and provides the foundation for Affirm’s mission to deliver honest financial products.

About the role

Affirm is seeking a Compliance Manager to own compliance advisory for the Affirm Card program. You'll make independent, risk-based calls across card marketing, onboarding, disputes, and remediation, partnering with Product, Engineering, and Operations to ship card features that are compliant and built to last.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end compliance advisory for the Affirm Card program, including card marketing, checkout, onboarding, wallets (Apple Pay, Google Pay), disputes, and servicing, partnering directly with Product, Engineering, and Operations throughout the development lifecycle

  • Bring an appetite for the unknown: much of what we build on Card is genuinely new and without precedent, and you take on that ambiguity rather than wait for a playbook

  • Apply sound judgment under EFTA (Reg E), TILA (Reg Z)/CARD Act, UDAAP, to navigate novel regulatory questions, escalating only where it's genuinely warranted

  • Review and approve Affirm Card marketing, disclosures, and UX to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and consistency with consumer protection standards

  • Lead root-cause analysis and remediation for Card compliance issues (e.g., disputes, adverse action notices, declines) through to sustainable closure, prioritizing durable fixes over one-off patches so issues don't recur

  • Partner with Compliance Testing, Legal, and Risk to prepare for and support regulatory exams and bank partner audits related to the Card program

  • Maintain and contribute to the Card program's compliance risk assessment and control inventory, proactively identifying and closing coverage gaps

  • Develop and maintain compliance training and reference materials specific to Card regulatory requirements

  • Serve as the go-to compliance expert on new and evolving Card features, surfacing risk early in the product lifecycle rather than after launch

What we look for

  • 8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory role within financial services with a Bachelor's degree (6+ years with a Master's degree, or 3+ years with a PhD, or equivalent), with meaningful experience on card, payments; compliance certifications a plus

  • Deep working knowledge of EFTA (Reg E) and TILA (Reg Z)/CARD Act as applied to card products, plus familiarity with TISA (Reg DD) and UDAAP; hands-on experience with card network rules (e.g., Visa, Mastercard) is a big plus

  • A demonstrated track record of operating independently in ambiguous, fast-paced environments, making sound, risk-based decisions with incomplete information and escalating only when it truly requires it

  • Comfortable partnering closely with Product from the early stages of a build, whether a new product, feature, or servicing program, in fast-paced, ambiguous environments

  • Experience owning issues from root-cause analysis through sustainable remediation, with a bias toward fixing the underlying control rather than the immediate symptom

  • Experience advising and building credibility with Product, Engineering, and Operations stakeholders on a card, lending, or payments program

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly present complex, nuanced regulatory issues to non-compliance audiences

  • Self-directed with strong strategic thinking and problem-solving skills; comfortable being the compliance voice in the room on card-specific questions, including presenting to senior leadership and leadership committees

  • Inquisitive and proactive in identifying problems and proposing practical, business-aware solutions

Base Pay Grade - L

Equity Grade - 6
